title: Progressive Output Observability: KV-window Anchoring and Contextual PII Scrub
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Goal: Provide deterministic, low-overhead observability for progressive (streamed) model outputs that ties per-fragment metrics to long-running traces while ensuring PII is scrubbed with context-aware heuristics. This ticket implements a KV-window anchoring concept to shard metrics across fragments, durable trace anchors that survive retries and tool/function-call handoffs, and a runtime sanitization pass for logs and telemetry derived from streamed content.
background: Current streaming telemetry captures chunk-level timings and token counts but lacks: 1) durable anchors to correlate fragments across retries and multi-stage tool calls; 2) consistent quantization windows for latency/cost aggregation (we often double-count in downstream dashboards); 3) an adaptive redaction strategy that can operate on partial outputs without over-scrubbing developer-visible debugging tokens. This causes noisy dashboards, missed regressions, and privacy risk in low-sampling channels.
proposed_solution: 1) KV-window anchoring: attach a lightweight 'kv_anchor' header to each streaming session representing the canonical KV-cache window id and sequence offset. Agents emitting metrics use kv_anchor + fragment_index to emit non-overlapping shard keys in metrics storage. 2) Trace anchoring: create a short-lived trace anchor span launched at stream start (span.kind=anchor) that child spans (per-fragment, tool-calls, function executions) attach to using stable correlation IDs. Anchors are re-emitted on resume/retry with the same correlation id. 3) Contextual PII scrub: add a small redact pipeline that uses (a) prompt/response pattern matching, (b) model score-based heuristics for name/ssn patterns, and (c) allowlist tokens. The scrub runs at two tiers: telemetry-only (aggressive) and debug-enabled (less aggressive, gated by dev token and audit log). Metrics emission is always from sanitized payloads unless opt-in for debug is present.
tradeoffs: Adding kv_anchor increases per-request header size slightly (approx 32-64 bytes) — acceptable versus duplication across metrics storage.
Trace anchors make spans easier to correlate but require instrumentation changes in tool/function calling layers; initial rollout will only support major platforms (node/python) then extend.
Contextual scrubbing risks false negatives/positives; dual-mode approach reduces developer pain but requires clear audit logs and opt-in for raw capture.
Sampling: to control cost we will sample full-text captures at 1% by default; this may miss rare regressions but keeps storage affordable.
acceptance_criteria: kv_anchor header appended to all streamed sessions in the hosted API and logged in request metadata
Per-fragment metrics emitted use composite key {kv_anchor, fragment_index} and show no cross-fragment double-count in dashboard aggregation
Anchor span created at stream start and child spans emitted by per-fragment processing, tool calls, and function runtime attach to anchor via correlation id
Contextual PII scrub applied to all telemetry-derived payloads; sample audit logs proving scrub effectiveness (precision/recall > 90% on test set)
End-to-end test harness demonstrating a resume/retry scenario preserves anchor id and merges metrics correctly
Feature flags present: streaming_observability.v2 (off by default) and streaming_observability.debug_capture (opt-in with audit trail)
technical_notes: Metric shard key: sha1(kv_anchor || ':' || fragment_index) to keep metric series cardinality bounded
kv_anchor generation: 128-bit random id salted by customer_id and creation_time to avoid collisions across customers
Trace anchors implemented as a parentless span with attribute anchor.id and anchor.fingerprint; use OpenTelemetry semantic conventions
Redaction pipeline built as a chainable filter with deterministic order: allowlist -> regex patterns -> ML-based classifier -> token-level mask
Runtime changes required: node SDK streaming client, python SDK client, runtime proxy to propagate kv_anchor header through tool/function call handoffs
Backward compatibility: when kv_anchor missing, fallback to existing chunk_id but mark metrics with legacy_shard=true
Storage implications: metrics ingestion will add a small tag; evaluate cardinality growth and roll up in the metrics ETL to hourly aggregates for high-cardinality streams
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): server-side support + node SDK instrumentation behind streaming_observability.v2 flag for 5% of traffic (internal dev orgs only)
Phase 2 (expand): enable python SDK + add anchor emission on tool/function runtimes; enable sampling audit logs for 1% of streams
Phase 3 (gradual): increase traffic coverage to 50% and monitor cardinality and cost; iterate on scrub heuristics
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default with conservative scrub rules; publish docs and SDK changelogs; provide migration guide for customers using custom metrics aggregation
test_plan: Unit tests for kv_anchor generation and deterministic shard key derivation
Integration test that simulates: stream start, emit fragments, trigger a retry, resume stream — assert anchor id stability and metric deduplication
Load test injecting high-fragment-rate streams to measure metric cardinality and ingestion cost impact
Privacy evaluation: run scrub pipeline against curated PII corpus (names, emails, SSNs, phone numbers, code snippets) and report precision/recall
End-to-end tracing test attaching Jaeger/OTEL collector to validate anchor span visible and child spans link correctly
E2E test with tool/function call chain: model -> tool A -> function execution -> model resume; assert anchor preserved and redaction applied at each hop
